title: Evolution experiment record
description:
One attempt at the change a batch's analysis called for: its identity, the batch base it starts from, its durable ref, its append-only rounds, the promotion it prepared, and the terminal decision that turns it into history (contract: Change lineage). This record — not `.ai-tasks/`, not a branch, not the checkout — is what makes an experiment discoverable, which is why it names its own task selections and candidate revisions rather than pointing at files that are machine-local or archived away.

Version 2 added the prepared promotion. A version-1 record is read against the frozen `experiment-v1.schema.json` and cannot carry one at all — including a version-1 promotion, which recorded the revision alone because that was the whole of what the operation writing it kept. That is why the field could not simply be made optional here: a reader with no version to go on cannot tell a promotion that recorded no merge unit from one that dropped it. For the same reason this version *requires* the key and spells "none prepared" as an explicit null — a record with no field at all is a version-1 record and nothing else, so the version answers the question rather than the record's completeness.

experiment_id.description: `<batch-id>-exp-<NN>`, one past the highest ordinal its batch has ever used. Never reused: a historical experiment's name has to keep naming the attempt it was. The ordinal is a positive number zero-padded to two digits and no wider than it needs to be, so one attempt has exactly one spelling — `00` names no attempt, and `01` and `001` would be two directories for one position in the series. The batch's ordinals run 1..N with none missing and only the newest still open, which the controller enforces across the records the way the schema enforces the spelling of each.

base_revision.description: The exact source commit this experiment starts from, frozen by the batch's first experiment. Every experiment of one batch carries the same value; a differing one is refused rather than reconciled (contract invariant 15).

base_release_ref.description: The most recent release tag reachable from `base_revision` at creation time, or null when the checkout had none. Recorded rather than re-derived so the record still states which released protocol this candidate builds on after the tag is gone (contract invariant 4 keeps missing fields explicit).

ref.description: The durable Git ref holding this experiment's rounds. Fast-forward only, so every pinned candidate revision stays reachable after the working branch is deleted.

rounds.description: Append-only. At most one round is unsealed, and it is the last one; every earlier round is candidate-ready and is never edited again.

round.description: One revision pass: the tasks admitted into it and the candidate it produced. Replay evidence names a round, so sealing one and opening the next is what makes prior evidence stale by construction.

reason.description: Why this round exists — the grouped admission for round 1, the revision reason afterwards.

seal.description: What makes a round candidate-ready, or null while it is still taking work. One object rather than two nullable fields so a half-pinned round — sealed with no revision, or a revision nobody sealed — is not a shape this contract can even hold (contract invariant 16). Nothing measures an unsealed round: the tip moves while a round is open, so evidence gathered before this record exists cannot say which tree it described.

sealed_at.description: When the controller sealed the round, having observed every admitted task complete. Not when the last task finished.

candidate_revision.description: The ref tip pinned at that moment: the revision replay exercises and every terminal decision names. Immutable, and the ref stays here until a new round is opened. Distinct from the promotion revision a promoted candidate later produces on the source line.

admitted_task.description: One draft's admission: which proposal it was, the bytes admitted, the task the copy took, and whether that task was seen through to completion. The hash is the provenance a copied draft would otherwise lose the moment either file is edited.

draft_id.description: The draft's stem under `batches/<batch-id>/proposed-tasks/`. A kebab slug, so it is one path segment with no traversal, no dot-file, and no extension to confuse for one. A draft may be consumed once; re-proposing the idea means a new id.

completion_observed_at.description: When this task was observed at `completed`, or null while it has not been. Recorded here because the observation is the only durable form of it: `.ai-tasks/` is machine-local and close-out archives a finished task away, so on any other clone the task's own status is unreadable rather than merely absent. A round is sealed only once every task it admitted carries this (contract invariant 16).

decision.description: The terminal decision, or null while the experiment is open. `superseded_by` is set only for `superseded` and `promotion_revision` only for `promoted`; both are present and null otherwise. `promoted` additionally requires the last round to be candidate-ready, since what was promoted is the revision that round pinned and not the tip as it stood at decision time; `abandoned` and `superseded` may end an experiment whose last round was never sealed, which is the honest record of an attempt dropped before it produced a candidate. The controller enforces all of that, which the implemented JSON Schema subset cannot express — the fields stay explicit rather than optional so a record never leaves the reader guessing whether a value is absent or unrecorded.

superseded_by.description: The experiment that replaced this one: the same batch, the same base, and the next ordinal in the series, because superseding creates its successor in the same operation. The controller refuses any other name — an earlier attempt, a record's own id, or one that does not exist — since none of them is a replacement it could have made.

promotion_revision.description: The source-line commit carrying this candidate's change. Never the candidate tip it came from.

promotion.description:
The merge unit this experiment's promotion was prepared as, written before the source line moved and never edited afterwards — so it is equally the record of what the promotion went as. Null means no promotion is prepared here, and it is stated: the key is required at this version, so a record that lost the field is refused rather than read as an experiment that never prepared one. What that refusal protects is the interval this field exists for — while the field is set, a merge this controller made may already be standing on the source line, and a reader that forgot it would let the experiment be ended, revised, or promoted a second time over that merge.

It exists because a promotion is two writes in another repository's terms — a commit, then a ref move — with the records that explain them arriving afterwards, and a run that stops in between has to be finishable. `revision` is that identity: the exact commit this operation made. A run coming back asks Git whether that commit is on the line, which admits a line that has taken further commits since (an ordinary advance, and the promotion is still on it) and refuses a commit that merely resembles this one. Recognising the merge by its shape instead — those parents, that tree — adopts anything shaped like it, including a merge a human made by hand, and cannot survive the line advancing at all.

That null is exact at this version: a record that ended `promoted` carries a merge unit, and one that ended any other way carries none. The implemented schema subset has no cross-field conditionals, so the controller holds a record to that pairing; what the schema states on its own is that this shape belongs to version 2, and that a promoted record written before the shape existed is a version-1 record read as the version-1 promotion it is.

round.description: The round whose seal pinned the promoted candidate — this experiment's last round, and no earlier one. The controller checks it against this record's own rounds: a merge unit naming a round this experiment never sealed describes a candidate nothing here produced, and one naming an earlier sealed round describes a candidate this experiment has already revised past. It is the last round rather than merely a sealed one because nothing may open a round while a promotion is prepared, so the round a promotion is prepared from is still the last one when it is recorded.

candidate_revision.description: The revision that round's seal pinned and replay exercised — the second parent of `revision`, and never `revision` itself.

merge_input_revision.description: Where the source line stood when this promotion was prepared: the first parent of `revision`, and the commit the replay integrated onto. What the ref move compares against, so a line that took a commit in between refuses rather than carrying an untested merge.

merge_input_ref.description: The source-line ref this promotion moves. Fully qualified, for the reason a replay's is: a bare name or a revision expression resolves against whichever working copy asks, and a run finishing this promotion elsewhere has to look at the same line.

tree.description: The tree `revision` carries, which is the tree the replay measured. What identifies the thing promoted: the same two commits merged with a different strategy, or with a conflict resolved by hand, land somewhere else.

revision.description: The merge commit this promotion made, recorded before the source line was moved to it. The whole of the operation's identity: an interrupted run is finished by finding this commit on the line, and one that never reached it is discarded rather than guessed at.

reason.description: Why the evidence justified the promotion. Recorded here as well as in the decision because this is written first, and a run finishing an interrupted promotion states the reason that was given rather than a new one.

planned_targets.description: The targets this promotion was intended for, held here so the outcome states the plan the promotion was made under rather than whatever a later retry happened to name. Same shape and same meaning as the batch outcome's — names, a plan, never an observation of what any target holds.

prepared_at.description: When the merge commit was made — before the ref moved and before any decision was recorded, which is why it is not the decision's moment.
